subject: Number of transects required for survey

messages.author: e7d892c85641663f
messages.subject: Number of transects required for survey
parts:
Could someone experienced with using Distance 5 software answer a question=20
for us?

What we would like to know is approximately how many transects to complete=20
to give us a reliable picture in Distance 5? Even a percentage of the=20
study area to cover will help our planning.

Some background information follows:

In four weeks time (mid-October) we will undertake a coastal survey in=20
Albania searching for sea turtles (Caretta caretta) and Mediterranean Monk=20
Seals (Monachus monachus). The project lasts about one month and will=20
operate from a small yacht. The main stakeholders are the Albanian=20
Ministry of the Environment, Tirana University, Medasset (Greece), and=20
TurtlePoint, Napoli (Italy).

We will be looking at different aspects at various times: 1) a record of=20
occasional sightings of turtles and Monk Seals along the entire Albanian=20
coast, 2) pinpoint possible Monk Seal Refuges, such as caves or remote=20
coves, 3) detailed habitat surveys at Karaburuni and Patok =96 these will=20
include SCUBA diving surveys for turtles and their habitats.

Sea turtles are captured in fishing gear along much of the Albanian coast,=20
but particularly in Patok Lagoon. The Albanian government wishes to=20
create a Marine Reserve at Karaburuni, and so our surveys will form part=20
of the inventory of species diversity.

Assuming that we find enough turtles we would like to use Distance 5 for=20
line transect data during our underwater surveys of turtle distribution=20
and abundance (Karaburuni and Patok). We have a usable technique for=20
photo-identification of individual loggerheads (using facial scales and=20
carapace scutes), and we would be able to measure the distance from a=20
transect line underwater to a turtle (even if we had to wait until the=20
animals swam off).

We have read the paper by Evans and Hammond (2004) for cetacean=20
monitoring, and found many useful points for survey design. Some=20
parameters that we have to contend with are: loggerhead turtles are mainly=20
solitary as juveniles and adults (some interactions do occur, mating being=20
the obvious one, but occasionally several animals may forage close to one=20
another on a particularly abundant food resource, such as crabs); turtles=20
are a migratory species throughout their lives; small juveniles tend to be=20
pelagic, larger turtles recruit into benthic habitats; they spend most=20
(90%) of their time submerged; they may show short-term fidelity to a=20
particular sea area for some weeks; much of their life cycle remains=20
unstudied. For diving sites the visibility may vary from day to day.

Thanks in advance,=20

Michael White, Marine Zoologist, Centro Recupero Tartarughe Marine, 92010=20
Lampedusa (AG), Italia.=20

messages.author: 4b4a7b00c1dd09c7
messages.subject: Re: Number of transects required for survey
parts:
Hi Vassilis, (cc list)

You should read chapter 7 of Introduction to Distance Sampling, which covers
survey design and field methods. There are some formulae in section 7.2.2
that can suggest a total transect length, given some pilot data or some
assumptions. These don't help you with number of transects however. As it
says in Section 7.2.1, you want a minimum of 10-20 transects (that is per
stratum). More than 20 gives you an even better picture of the true level of
spatial variation in density. If this variation is high, you need to think
about stratification to reduce variance.

There is also a whole chapter in the Advanced Distance Sampling book on
automated survey design and using the GIS facilities in Distance (chapter 7).

Hope this helps!

- len
